assessments.rationale: Both are the primary artifact being created; the house is the physical product, the software is the digital product. The roles (object of design) align directly.
Occupants experience and use the house just as users interact with a software system; the relationship of 'consumer of the artifact' matches.

assessments.source_element: Light switch placed next to the door for easy discovery in the dark
assessments.rationale: Discoverability of a control in a physical environment maps cleanly onto discoverability of interface elements; the principle of making essential functions easy to locate is central to usability.

assessments.source_element: Wide hallways that allow comfortable movement and prevent doors from colliding
assessments.target_element: Interaction design (design of interactions to avoid conflicts)
assessments.rationale: Designing space to prevent physical interference mirrors designing interaction flows to avoid functional conflicts; the analogy preserves the causal role of layout in smooth operation.

assessments.source_element: House feeling like a home—comfortable and intuitive
assessments.target_element: User experience (overall feeling of comfort and intuition)
assessments.rationale: Overall affective quality of a living space corresponds directly to the affective quality of a digital product; both capture holistic user satisfaction.

result.rationale: All source-to-target correspondences preserve the roles, relations, and mechanisms described in HCI. The mappings are logically coherent and do not require unsupported leaps, justifying a high score of 2 with strong confidence.
